ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two objects A and B of equal mass are pressed closely against the vertical inner wall of a uniformly rotating cylinder and make uniform circular motion together with the cylinder; then which of the following relations is correct
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The resultant forces on them satisfy F_A resultant > F_B resultant

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, two objects A and B of equal mass are pressed closely against the vertical inner wall of a uniformly rotating cylinder and make uniform circular motion together with the cylinder. What is the magnitude relationship of the resultant forces on objects A and B?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The resultant forces on them satisfy F_A resultant > F_B resultant
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a vertical rotation axis passing through the inside of the cylinder, and below there is a curved arrow indicating rotation; two small objects A and B are pressed against the vicinity of the vertical inner wall on the left side of the cylinder. The position of A is farther left than B, so the distance from A to the vertical rotation axis is larger, and the distance from B to the rotation axis is smaller, namely r_A>r_B. Then reason: The stem states that A and B have equal masses and make uniform circular motion together with the same uniformly rotating cylinder, so their angular velocities ω are the same. The objects have no acceleration in the vertical direction, and gravity and static friction are balanced in the vertical direction; the resultant force on them is just the resultant force in the horizontal direction that provides centripetal acceleration, with magnitude F resultant=mω²r. Since m is the same, ω is the same, and r_A>r_B, F_A resultant>F_B resultant.
